title: ORCHES: Orchestrated Test-Time-Compute-based LLM Reasoning on Collaborative GPU-PIM HEterogeneous System
problem: Test-time compute (TTC) inference pipelines for LLM reasoning on edge devices suffer from three bottlenecks: variable parallelism due to inference-dependent dynamic control flow and varying batch sizes; branch dependencies that stall sequential reasoning steps; and branch pruning causing memory fragmentation and irregular access patterns.
motivation: TTC-based reasoning with compact LLMs offers strong potential for edge AI, but current GPU implementations are inefficient due to the memory-bound nature of LLMs and the highly irregular, branching inference control flow that GPUs are not optimized to handle.
method: ORCHES is a GPU-PIM collaborative system that partitions LLM reasoning workloads between a GPU and Processing-in-Memory (PIM) units. Three key mechanisms address the identified bottlenecks: (1) adaptive workload assignment dynamically balances computation between GPU and PIM based on real-time branching patterns; (2) branch-aware pipelining uses speculative execution to overlap reasoning steps and reduce inter-step pipeline stalls from branch dependencies; (3) fragmentation-aware memory structuring improves data locality through coordinated caching strategies and optimized memory layout reorganization to handle irregular access caused by branch pruning.
key_novelty: Branch-aware pipelining with speculative execution specifically designed for TTC reasoning control flow, combined with adaptive GPU-PIM workload splitting that responds to dynamic branching at inference time.
contributions: Identification and characterization of three efficiency barriers in TTC-based LLM reasoning: variable parallelism, branch dependencies, and memory fragmentation
Adaptive GPU-PIM workload assignment that dynamically balances compute despite unpredictable branching
Branch-aware pipelining via speculative execution to reduce inter-step pipeline stalls
4.16x and 3.10x average speedup over SOTA GPU for text-based and vision-based TTC reasoning respectively

metrics.speedup: 4.16x over SOTA GPU (text-based TTC reasoning); 3.10x over SOTA GPU (vision-based TTC reasoning)

baselines: state-of-the-art GPU implementations of TTC reasoning
limitations: Not discussed; evaluation scope (edge device type, specific PIM architecture model) is not detailed in the abstract.
primary_theme: GPU-PIM collaborative system for test-time-compute LLM reasoning
